high.title: Short and Intermediate DI Rates Fall as Bets on Selic Rate Cut Increase
high.summary: Short and intermediate DI (Interbank Deposit) rates retreated on Friday as market participants increased their bets that the Banco Central do Brasil (BCB) is moving toward another Selic rate cut at its August COPOM meeting. Longer-dated rates ended the session broadly flat. The benchmark DI rate for January 2028 fell 11 basis points to 14.14%, reflecting growing conviction among fixed income traders that the easing cycle still has room to continue. An additional contributing factor was the pullback in international oil prices, which reduced inflationary pressure expectations and gave the BCB additional room to maneuver on the dovish side.

medium.title: Real Estate Fund in Liquidation and Tesouro IPCA+ at 10%: See What Caught the Most Attention This Week
medium.summary:
The week's key highlights include the cancellation of a Tesouro Nacional bond auction, with the market pricing the IPCA+ government bond (inflation-linked Tesouro Direto instrument) at close to a 10% real yield — a notably elevated level that signals persistent inflation risk premium and/or fiscal concern in long-dated Brazilian sovereign debt. The Treasury's decision to cancel the auction may reflect an attempt to avoid locking in high borrowing costs at elevated yield levels, a tactically significant move for fixed income market participants. Additional items covered include a real estate fund entering liquidation and a share buyback by Klabin (KLBN11). For international bond investors, the IPCA+ yield level approaching 10% is a critical data point, suggesting the market continues to demand a high risk premium on Brazilian inflation-linked paper, which has direct implications for sovereign debt sustainability narratives and BRL sentiment.
